section_summary: This section continues a report on Japan’s 1947 elections. It describes the political effects of the public office purge, police instructions to avoid election interference, and Occupation procedures for observing campaigns, polling, and vote counting.

subfiles.title: Report on the 1947 Japanese elections and Occupation surveillance
subfiles.about: Assesses the effects of the public office purge and explains police and Occupation measures to ensure fair elections.
subfiles.summary: The report gives screening figures, names prominent politicians purged in April 1947, and compares the losses suffered by political parties. It recounts Home Ministry instructions requiring impartial police conduct and reports that police performance drew no complaints. It then describes SCAP’s surveillance planning, quotes detailed instructions to military government officers, and explains how teams observed campaigns and elections while referring violations to Japanese authorities.
